top_findings.title: Standings double-counts overlapping Brasileirão data: duplicate club rows and doubled game counts
top_findings.evidence: src/lib.rs:316 standings() computes points from matches (not hardcoded, so R9's mechanism IS present), but src/lib.rs:331 groups by the raw team string with no normalization while Database::load (src/lib.rs:56 + src/lib.rs:90) concatenates Brasileirao_Matches.csv AND novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv — both labelled 'Brasileirão', both carrying all 380 rows of the 2019 Série A season, and find_matches' competition filter (src/lib.rs:218 contains()) matches both. Verified against the bundled data: the two files' 2019 team-name strings union to 39 distinct rows (only 'Botafogo-RJ' is byte-identical across both, so its counts add to 76 played on 38 real games; every other club splits into two rows, e.g. 'Flamengo-RJ' and 'Flamengo' each showing 38 played). standings(2019,'Brasileirão') therefore returns a 39-row table for a 20-team league.
top_findings.suggestion: Dedup the two Brasileirão sources (or drop the overlapping seasons on load) and normalize the group-by key in standings() the same way same_team()/normalize() already do elsewhere. Add a standings test — it is the only query capability with no test.
